By merging IGIOWO’s unparalleled research with KJC’s implementation expertise, we deliver systems that redefine performance, security, and resilience.
Core Technologies: Leading the Quantum Revolution

At the core of modern systems lies the need for ultra-precise timing. QuantumSync delivers sub-nanosecond synchronization, redefining benchmarks in:
•	Aerospace: Real-time satellite coordination and deep-space navigation.
•	Finance: High-frequency trading with unprecedented speed and accuracy.
•	Defense: Secure GPS-denied operations for critical missions.
•	EV and Smart Grids: High-precision energy management.
Why It’s Revolutionary:
QuantumSync ensures operational continuity in the harshest environments, from hypersonic aircraft to submarine depths.
Prototype Note: Currently in development, QuantumSync represents the next phase in quantum sub nano-second precision synchronization, with game-changing potential for aerospace, defense and commercial use.

•	Hypersonic Environments: Navigation and communication under extreme speeds and thermal conditions.
•	Submarine Operations: Secure acoustic data transmission and power transfer.
•	Radiation-Hardened Applications: Reliable performance in high-radiation zones, such as space or nuclear facilities.

•	Combines military-grade resilience with commercial scalability.
•	Ensures seamless integration across terrestrial and space platforms.
Prototype Note: Currently in development, iROSE represents the next phase in quantum versatility, with game-changing potential for aerospace, defense and commercial use.

QuantumMESH introduces a distributed quantum-optical mesh network designed for secure, high-speed communication. Its innovation lies in adaptive, self-healing satellite constellations that integrate:
1.	Quantum Key Distribution (QKD): Unbreakable security for data in transit.
2.	Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG): Network-wide entropy distribution for secure randomness.
3.	AI-Driven Network Optimization: Real-time routing adjustments based on operational demands.
Applications:
•	Ensures secure connectivity in mission-critical operations.
•	Supports both terrestrial and orbital platforms.

Disaitek’s mission:

Disaitek is dedicated to combating environmental damage and climate change by leveraging advanced Earth Observation and AI technologies.

Background: 

- Originating from space observation, Disaitek developed the first deep learning technology to detect variable orbital period exoplanets, validated by NASA and included in the Kepler database.

- Since 2021, our focus has shifted to Earth observation to address environmental issues.

Core achievements: 

Littering and illegal landfills detection platform: We have built the first platform that automates the detection and the monitoring of littering and illegal landfills with very high resolution imagery and AI. This task has been very challenging to tackle as it akin to anomaly detection and no dataset on the topic exists. Desplite this, it is now an operational platform with several customers and has been in production since mid-2022.
Canal Seine Nord Europe project: Awarded a contract with the Canal Seine Nord Europe, the largest civil engineering work of the decade in Europe, to monitor the progress and the environmental impact of the work, with satellite imagery and AI. For this we use optical VHR mono and stereo and SAR time series data. 

Technological expertise: 
Utilizing very high-resolution optical imagery, hyperspectral, and SAR time series.
Expertise in complex SAR stacks for producing interferometric products.
Developed a foundation model with high-resolution images and self-supervised learning for advanced land cover classification.

Team composition: 

Our team consists predominantly of PhDs in astrophysics, climate physics, and computer science.

Awards and recognition:

June 2023: Disaitek won the Paris Saclay Spring 50 Best Startup award in the New Space category 
October 2023: Disaitek won the Assises Nationales des Déchets award in the Technological Breakthrough category.
June 2024: Achieved 2nd place in the European Earth Observation award by EARSC, for the most innovative value-added product supporting the Green Deal agenda and Sustainable Development.

CNR-ISAFOM (Institute for Agriculture and FOrestry Systems in the Mediterranean) is a research institute of the National Research Council of Italy focused on sustainable agricultural and forestry practices in Mediterranean climates.
It conducts studies on the impacts of climate change, particularly related to crop production and forest management. The institute combines various research areas, including agronomy, forestry, ecology, and hydrology, to develop solutions for sustainable land use. The aim is to improve both the quantity and quality of agricultural and forestry production, optimize the use of natural resources, and enhance the functions of agricultural and forest systems. This also involves developing and applying advanced research methods and technological innovations for monitoring and predicting the impacts and responses of agricultural and forest ecosystems to anthropogenic and climatic pressures.

Obuda University (OU), established in 1879, is the second largest but highest ranked Technical University in Hungary. It aims to achieve the triplet of excellence in education, research, and innovation to address societal challenges and contribute to sustainable development on national, regional and EU level. OU has seven faculties and three doctoral schools, one excellence centre, and eight research labs. OU is participating in multiple international organizations and bilateral and international programmes (currently over 20 EU financed scientific projects). It has international relations with 90 countries, and participates 300 higher education programs and partnerships and has over 250 education and mobility agreements. OU offers innovative BA/BSc, MA/MSC, and PhD curricula, dual degrees, challenge-based approaches and an up-to-date, student-friendly, creative and supporting environment for students in order to enable them respond to the challenges set out by our globalized world, laying emphasis on both basic and applied research, internationalization, sustainable development, improvements in technology, RDI, lifelong learning, and interaction and cooperation with the industry. In the last 10 years, OU’s research is expanding into fields that are in the major problem areas of today’s societies: health and sustainability. ÓU’s mission and vision are underpinned by fundamental values such as nurturing entrepreneurship, openness, tolerance, dialogue and diversity to fulfil its responsibility as a higher education institution contributing to positive societal change.
Mission
The fundamental mission of the University is to serve the interest of society, the economy and our industrial partners through the transfer and constant development of high level knowledge and skills and innovation.
Vision/Core values
The highest value of the university are its students, as well as its qualified professionals, engineers, computer scientists, economists, engineering teachers and doctors who provide the trademark of the University. A key task in education is to improve students’ critical thinking skills to develop initiative, tolerant, empathetic behaviour, professionalism, creativity, entrepreneurship, national affiliation and relationship-building skills as well as a strong personality.
The main aim of the University is to develop a new, multifaceted model of higher education. A university that offers a network-based approach, practice-oriented, industry-oriented, high-level higher education vocational training, undergraduate, master’s and doctoral programs, as well as a wide range of international research and development and innovation activities to responsibly serve the needs of the society nationally, regionally and globally through educating the next generation of global citizens.
The University continuously develops its activities in the form of project-based education based on real corporate tasks and the establishment of incubator units by cooperating with key players of the economy and the local communities, the companies, their research sites and laboratories. The improvement of the internationalization in both education and research is of high priority at Obuda University.

entityDescription:
The Chair of Space Mobility and Propulsion at TUM advances sustainable and innovative space technologies. Its research spans propulsion systems, in-space mobility, and resource-efficient systems like water electrolysis and solar-thermal propulsion. Focus areas include reusable and throttleable space propulsion systems for access to space and landing capabilities, in-space propulsion for autonomy and sustainability, advanced control systems leveraging AI and ML models. The team integrates teaching, experimental projects, and real-world applications, including the ASCENT rocket hopper and SPARK initiatives. These efforts focus on advancing propulsion and mobility solutions to enable future space missions. Explore more:

UAB SPACEUNION is focused on the counter-drone cutting edge lase-based technologies for detection of unauthorized drones, identification, tracking and neutralization by LASER DIRECTED ENERGY weapons to disable or intercept rogue drones. 
Those disruptive C-UAV solutions can aslo be used not only in military sector but for increasing the resilience of critical infrastructure contribute in improving monitoring, risk assessment, forecast, mitigation and modelling techniques aimed at increasing the resilience of critical infrastructures, also of border and customs facility, validating multi-hazard scenarios, creating interactive hazard maps supported by Earth Observation and other data sources.

SPACEUNION Anti-Drone Solutions are thus a great tool against exploitation attacks, protecting borders against attacks, penetrations, and smuggling with radar capability up to 3km detection range for small UAV’s (up to 50cm diagonal) and up to 5 km for UAV with diagonal 1,0m and more. For some application like preventing intelligence activities or smuggling of goods using balloons, we are deploying special solution –“laser drone” with the low power. When such a threat is detected by the radar, a “laser drone” is sent to the given coordinates and burns through the shell so that the balloon lands vertically down. This solution is also quite effective in combating reconnaissance FPV drones. When such targets are detected, the “laser drone”, operator directs the laser beam to the video camera and blinds it.
